one_liner: Plain is a B2B support platform with a full-parity GraphQL API, machine-user API keys, OAuth apps, and an official OAuth-based hosted MCP server. API use appears to require a paid workspace.
auth_notes: OAuth apps (authorization code, with PKCE for client-side apps and a client secret for server-side apps) call the API as the signed-in user. Machine users hold API keys, sent as Bearer plainApiKey_xxx, with fine-grained permissions. Webhooks use HMAC-SHA256 request signing and mTLS, which is OTHER.
access_notes: The evidence shows only paid plans (Foundation $45/user/month billed annually, Horizon $99, Frontier custom). It shows no free tier or free trial. Machine-user API keys are created in workspace settings, so a paid workspace is probably needed. This is inferred, not stated.
blocker_notes: There is no evidence of a free tier or trial, so a paid workspace is likely needed for testing. Otherwise the API is well documented, with a published GraphQL schema and self-serve OAuth apps.

evidence.quote: Click “Add API key” and select the permissions you need.
